topic: Project Status Record: Aiko Watanabe, Gary Marks

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Section 3. You will hear two business students talking to their tutor about a research project on flexible work policies.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: First, you have some time to read through questions 9 to 13.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Now, listen carefully and answer questions 9 to 13.

transcript.speaker: Tutor
transcript.text: I'm interested in hearing how your research on alternative work place policies. The last time we talked, you said you were going to focus on flex place and flex time?

transcript.speaker: Tutor
transcript.text: So, what progress have you made?

transcript.speaker: Gary
transcript.text: Well, I looked through some case studies I found in the library showing that flex time policies, which basically let employees decide what hours they work, allow for less fatigue and illness. In addition, motivation among company workers was increased, and people were more enthusiastic about their work.
transcript.highlight_text: In addition, motivation among company workers was increased

transcript.speaker: Tutor
transcript.text: What conclusion did the studies reach?

transcript.speaker: Gary
transcript.text: It seems flex time is really great for employees, actually. They can adapt their work hours to public transportation schedules and road traffic, and even more importantly, they have opportunities to spend more time with their children. So, their work-life balance is greatly improved.
transcript.highlight_text: So, their work-life balance is greatly improved.

transcript.speaker: Gary
transcript.text: I've discovered that, with flex time, parents don't have to give up their jobs to raise their kids. This has been a great advantage for mothers and fathers with very young children.

transcript.speaker: Tutor
transcript.text: That's all good. You should research more about how flex time has benefited employers since the project must cover that as well. I think you have enough material on employees' viewpoints. Could you add some details about that to your analysis?
transcript.highlight_text: You should research more about how flex time has benefited employers

transcript.speaker: Gary
transcript.text: Absolutely. And I'll read through some other studies I found proving that flex time employees make fewer errors and are more effective.

transcript.speaker: Tutor
transcript.text: Great. Now, Aiko, to come back to you, have you found any similar results with regard to flex place?

transcript.speaker: Aiko
transcript.text: Well, there aren't as many case studies available about flex place, and it's a more recent phenomenon. I thought flex place would be inconvenient for workers, but I found out that increases in both wireless internet access and laptop affordability have made working from different locations more practical.
transcript.highlight_text: have made working from different locations more practical.

transcript.speaker: Tutor
transcript.text: Sure, but I want you to look a bit more deeply into flex place than that. I know there are several companies in London offering flex place programs. Since you don't have many previously conducted company studies to rely on, how about interviewing some of their recruitment staff?
transcript.highlight_text: how about interviewing some of their recruitment staff?

transcript.speaker: Aiko
transcript.text: Oh, alright. That's an excellent idea. I'll do some research online and see what companies I can find.

transcript.speaker: Tutor
transcript.text: Sounds good. And can you both send me a draft of your research report this week? Then let's meet again next Wednesday so I can give you some additional feedback on your findings.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You now have 15 seconds to check your answers.
